title: The Price of Candour
text:
Professional responsibility extends well beyond the strict fulfilment of contractual obligations. A physician who withholds a diagnosis to spare a patient distress, for instance, may believe they are acting compassionately, yet they deprive the patient of the autonomy to make informed decisions. Ethicists therefore argue that honesty, even when painful, is a precondition of genuine trust. The tension between kindness and candour rarely admits of easy resolution.

Responsibility also has a collective dimension that individuals often overlook. When an organisation tolerates a culture of concealment, the misconduct of a few employees can be attributed to everyone who remained silent. Whistleblowers, who expose such failings at considerable personal cost, are frequently portrayed as disloyal, although they arguably fulfil a more fundamental duty. Ultimately, ethical conduct depends less on rules than on the willingness to bear the consequences of one's choices.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, why might a physician withhold a diagnosis?
options: Because the law explicitly requires it

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, why are whistleblowers frequently portrayed negatively?
options: They break company rules for personal profit

questions.text: What does the author imply about the relationship between rules and ethical conduct?
options: Rules are the only reliable guide to ethics
Written rules alone cannot guarantee ethical behaviour
Ethical conduct is unrelated to personal choice
Rules should be abandoned in professional settings

questions.text: Why does the author describe honesty as a precondition of genuine trust?
options: Because honesty is always pleasant to hear
Because trust cannot exist without a reliable disclosure of truth
Because patients prefer doctors who conceal facts
Because contracts always require total honesty

vocabulary.definition: the freedom to make your own decisions
the quality of being open and honest
not supporting a person or group one is expected to support

paragraph_translations: La responsabilidad profesional se extiende mucho más allá del cumplimiento estricto de las obligaciones contractuales. Un médico que retiene un diagnóstico para evitarle angustia al paciente, por ejemplo, puede creer que actúa con compasión, pero le priva de la autonomía para tomar decisiones informadas. Por eso, los especialistas en ética sostienen que la honestidad, incluso cuando duele, es condición previa de una confianza genuina. La tensión entre la bondad y la franqueza rara vez admite una solución sencilla.

La responsabilidad también tiene una dimensión colectiva que a menudo pasamos por alto. Cuando una organización tolera una cultura de ocultación, la conducta indebida de unos pocos empleados puede atribuirse a todos los que permanecieron en silencio. Los denunciantes, que exponen esas faltas a un coste personal considerable, suelen ser presentados como desleales, aunque cabe argumentar que cumplen un deber más fundamental. En última instancia, la conducta ética depende menos de las normas que de la disposición a asumir las consecuencias de las propias decisiones.
